name: Spin-orbit coupling and Thomas precession
summary: An electron moving through an electric field sees a magnetic field B' = -v x E/c^2 in its rest frame; with the Thomas precession factor 1/2 this gives the spin-orbit coupling behind Rashba, Dresselhaus and spin Hall effects used in spintronics.
sources: Thomas (1926). "The Motion of the Spinning Electron". *Nature* 117, 514. [doi:10.1038/117514a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/117514a0)

name: Spinning black holes power AGN jets
summary: AGN engines are accreting Kerr black holes (Lynden-Bell 1969). In the Blandford–Znajek process, an electromagnetic version of the Penrose process, magnetic field lines threading the frame-dragged horizon extract its rotational energy and launch relativistic jets.
sources: Lynden-Bell (1969). "Galactic Nuclei as Collapsed Old Quasars". *Nature* 223, 690. [doi:10.1038/223690a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/223690a0)

name: Stellar-mass black holes as end states of collapse
summary: Above the maximum neutron-star mass (~2.2–2.3 M_sun) no pressure can halt collapse, so heavy stellar cores become Kerr black holes. X-ray binaries such as Cyg X-1 are where the GR geometry meets measured masses, spins inferred from the ISCO, and the lower mass gap at 2–5 M_sun.

name: Black-hole shadow as extreme gravitational lensing
summary: The EHT ring is the strong-deflection limit of lensing. Rays with impact parameters near b_c=√27 GM/c² wind around the photon sphere, forming the shadow edge and nested photon subrings, each demagnified by ~e^{−π} in Schwarzschild. The same deflection law gives Einstein rings in the weak-field limit.

name: Black-hole demographics and host-galaxy scaling
summary: Nearly every massive galaxy hosts a central black hole whose mass tracks its bulge, as in the M–σ relation. Black-hole masses from horizon-scale imaging and from stellar and gas dynamics calibrate these scaling relations, from Sgr A* to M87*.
sources: Kormendy & Ho (2013). "Coevolution (Or Not) of Supermassive Black Holes and Host Galaxies". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 51, 511. [arXiv:1304.7762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7762)

name: M87*: horizon-scale image of an AGN engine
summary: The EHT image of M87*, the core of a radio-loud AGN with a kiloparsec jet, shows a ~42 μas ring that matches the Kerr shadow of a 6.5×10⁹ M_sun black hole. GRMHD accretion and jet models are scored directly against the image and its polarisation.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Sgr A*: the Galactic Centre black hole
summary: Decades of S-star orbits weigh Sgr A* at ~4×10⁶ M_sun, and in 2022 the EHT imaged it as a ~52 μas ring consistent with a Kerr shadow. The two methods give independent mass-to-distance ratios, and they agree.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2022). "First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole in the Center of the Milky Way". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 930, L12. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac6674)

Ghez et al. (2008). "Measuring Distance and Properties of the Milky Way's Central Supermassive Black Hole with Stellar Orbits". *Astrophys. J.* 689, 1044. [arXiv:0808.2870](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2870)

name: de Sitter horizon thermodynamics
summary: In a Λ-dominated universe each observer has a cosmological event horizon with the Gibbons–Hawking temperature ħH/(2πk_B) and an area entropy, obeying the same laws as black-hole horizons. For our H₀ this gives T~10⁻³⁰ K and S~10¹²² k_B, the maximum entropy of the observable universe.
map: T_{\rm dS}=\frac{\hbar H}{2\pi k_B},\quad S_{\rm dS}=\frac{k_BA}{4\ell_P^2}=\frac{\pi k_Bc^5}{G\hbar H^2}

name: Hawking evaporation bounds primordial-black-hole DM
summary: Primordial black holes lighter than ~5×10¹¹ kg would have evaporated by today, and slightly heavier ones would still emit Hawking gamma rays and e±. Gamma-ray, 511 keV-line and CMB data therefore exclude PBHs as all of the dark matter below ~10¹⁴ kg, leaving the asteroid-mass window open.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Black-hole superradiance constrains ultralight bosons
summary: Bosons whose Compton wavelength is comparable to a Kerr black hole's size form gravitational 'atoms' that grow by superradiance while ω<mΩ_H, draining the hole's spin. Measured spins of stellar and supermassive black holes exclude some ultralight-boson mass ranges, and the clouds should emit monochromatic gravitational waves.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: ISCO sets the radiative efficiency of accretion
summary: A thin accretion disk radiates the binding energy at the innermost stable circular orbit. Its efficiency η=1−E_ISCO rises from 5.7% for Schwarzschild (r=6GM/c²) to 42% for maximal prograde Kerr. Soltan's argument, comparing integrated quasar light with the relic SMBH mass density, uses η to infer typical spins.

name: Cosmology is GR applied to the whole universe
summary: Modern cosmology is general relativity with a homogeneous, isotropic source. The Einstein equations with Λ and the FLRW ansatz give the Friedmann equations that ΛCDM fits to CMB, BAO and supernova data, so every cosmological test is also a large-scale test of GR.
map:

u}= rac{8\pi G}{c^4}T_{\mu
u}\Rightarrow H^2= rac{8\pi G}{3}ho- rac{kc^2}{a^2}+ rac{\Lambda c^2}{3}
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: TOV equation and the neutron-star maximum mass
summary: Relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium, the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equation from the Einstein equations with a perfect-fluid source, sets neutron-star structure. Because pressure itself gravitates, every equation of state has a maximum mass, and the Buchdahl bound caps compactness at 2GM/(Rc²) < 8/9.
sources: Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

name: Structure growth from linearised Einstein equations
summary: Cosmological perturbation theory is the Einstein equations linearised about FLRW. In Newtonian gauge the 00 component gives a Poisson equation for the Bardeen potential, and sub-horizon matter obeys a growth equation whose solution D(a) and growth rate f≈Ω_m^{0.55} are what BAO and RSD surveys measure.
sources: Eisenstein et al. (2005). "Detection of the Baryon Acoustic Peak in the Large-Scale Correlation Function of SDSS Luminous Red Galaxies". *Astrophys. J.* 633, 560. [arXiv:astro-ph/0501171](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0501171)

name: FLRW metric: the exact solution behind expansion
summary: The Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric is the exact solution for a homogeneous, isotropic universe, and de Sitter is its Λ-dominated limit. Its scale factor a(t) defines redshift, the distance measures and the expansion history H(z) that cosmology fits.

name: Dark energy or modified gravity?
summary: Cosmic acceleration can sit on the right side of Einstein's equations, as a dark-energy fluid with w≈−1, or on the left, as f(R), Horndeski or massive gravity. The two are degenerate in H(z) and are told apart by the growth of structure and lensing; any modification must also be screened to pass Solar-System tests.
sources: Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)

name: Gravitational slip: lensing vs dynamics tests GR
summary: Light responds to Φ+Ψ, while galaxies and peculiar velocities respond to Ψ alone. GR without anisotropic stress requires Φ=Ψ, so combining weak lensing with redshift-space distortions (the E_G statistic, slip η, μ–Σ parametrisations) tests modified gravity on Mpc–Gpc scales.

name: Starobinsky R² inflation is f(R) gravity
summary: The action f(R)=R+R²/(6M²) is conformally equivalent to GR plus a scalar field with a plateau potential. It drives inflation with n_s≈1−2/N and r≈12/N², inside Planck's preferred region, so the earliest successful inflation model is a modified-gravity theory.
sources: Starobinsky (1980). "A new type of isotropic cosmological models without singularity". *Phys. Lett. B* 91, 99. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X)
Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)

name: MOND needs a relativistic modified-gravity completion
summary: MOND modifies Newtonian dynamics below a₀≈1.2×10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻². To predict lensing and the CMB it needs a relativistic completion such as TeVeS or AeST, which places it among scalar–vector–tensor modified-gravity theories. GW170817 falsified the original TeVeS, which had gravitons and photons travelling on different metrics.
sources: Milgrom (1983). "A modification of the Newtonian dynamics as a possible alternative to the hidden mass hypothesis". *Astrophys. J.* 270, 365. [doi:10.1086/161130](https://doi.org/10.1086/161130)

name: GW170817's speed of gravity prunes dark-energy models
summary: The 1.7 s delay between GW170817 and GRB 170817A over ~40 Mpc fixes the speed of gravity to within ~10⁻¹⁵ of c. That eliminates the Horndeski and beyond-Horndeski dark-energy models whose tensor speed differs from c on cosmological backgrounds, including quartic and quintic galileons.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: Light deflection: from 1919 eclipse to lensing
summary: The GR deflection angle 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value and weighted by the PPN factor (1+γ)/2, is the kernel of the lens equation. The 1919 eclipse test grew into Einstein rings, cosmic shear and time-delay cosmography, and comparing lensing with dynamics tests γ on galactic scales.
sources: Dyson, Eddington & Davidson (1920). "A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field, from Observations Made at the Total Eclipse of May 29, 1919". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A* 220, 291. [doi:10.1098/rsta.1920.0009](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1920.0009)

name: S2's orbit tests GR near Sgr A*
summary: Adaptive-optics astrometry and spectroscopy of the star S2 detected the combined gravitational redshift and transverse Doppler shift at its 2018 pericentre, and later the prograde Schwarzschild precession of its orbit. This carries tests of GR to the potential of a 4×10⁶ M_sun black hole.
sources: GRAVITY Collaboration (2018). "Detection of the gravitational redshift in the orbit of the star S2 near the Galactic centre massive black hole". *Astron. Astrophys.* 615, L15. [arXiv:1807.09409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.09409)

name: Solar-System ephemerides as tests of GR
summary: Mercury's anomalous 43″ per century perihelion advance was GR's first success. Modern planetary ephemerides, built from radar, spacecraft tracking and lunar laser ranging, must include 1PN terms, and their fits bound the PPN parameters β and γ to ~10⁻⁵ along with the Nordtvedt effect and Ġ/G.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Binary pulsars: strong-field GR laboratories
summary: Pulsars in tight binaries, such as the Hulse–Taylor system and the Double Pulsar, yield post-Keplerian parameters: periastron advance, Shapiro delay and orbital decay. These test GR's quadrupole formula to better than 0.1% and weigh neutron stars, including the ~2 M_sun Shapiro-delay masses that constrain the equation of state.
sources: Hulse & Taylor (1975). "Discovery of a pulsar in a binary system". *Astrophys. J.* 195, L51. [doi:10.1086/181708](https://doi.org/10.1086/181708)

name: Solar oblateness and the perihelion test
summary: The Sun's quadrupole J₂ also advances Mercury's perihelion. Dicke and Goldenberg's 1967 oblateness claim (J₂~2.5×10⁻⁵) would have spoiled GR's 43″ and favoured Brans–Dicke theory. Helioseismic inversions of solar rotation later fixed J₂≈2.2×10⁻⁷, a negligible correction.
sources: Christensen-Dalsgaard (2002). "Helioseismology". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1073. [arXiv:astro-ph/0207403](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0207403)
Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Standard sirens: H₀ without a distance ladder
summary: A compact-binary waveform gives the luminosity distance directly from its amplitude and chirp, with no distance-ladder calibration. With a host-galaxy redshift, GW170817 gave H₀=70^{+12}_{−8} km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. Tens to hundreds of sirens could become an independent arbiter of the Hubble tension.
sources: Abbott et al. (2017). "A gravitational-wave standard siren measurement of the Hubble constant". *Nature* 551, 85. [arXiv:1710.05835](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05835)

name: Compact mergers as high-energy engines
summary: The compact-object mergers that GW detectors see also produce short GRBs and kilonovae, and are candidate sources of neutrinos and cosmic rays. GW triggers therefore drive joint searches with gamma-ray, X-ray and neutrino observatories.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: GW170817 opened GW multi-messenger astronomy
summary: The binary-neutron-star merger GW170817 was followed 1.7 s later by GRB 170817A and then by a kilonova across the spectrum. This one event confirmed that neutron-star mergers make short GRBs and produce r-process elements.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
LIGO, Virgo et al. (2017). "Multi-messenger Observations of a Binary Neutron Star Merger". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L12. [arXiv:1710.05833](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05833)

name: Pair-instability gap in the BH mass spectrum
summary: Stellar evolution predicts few black holes between ~50 and ~130 M_sun, because pair-instability supernovae disrupt helium cores in that range. GW catalogues test this prediction. GW190521's ~85 M_sun component lies inside the gap, pointing to hierarchical mergers or uncertain ¹²C(α,γ) rates.
sources: Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)

name: Primordial gravitational waves and CMB B-modes
summary: Tensor perturbations, the gravitational waves from inflation, create a quadrupolar anisotropy at last scattering. Thomson scattering turns it into curl-type B-mode polarisation, which scalar modes cannot make at linear order. The tensor-to-scalar ratio is bounded to r<0.036, and lensing B-modes are the main foreground.

name: GW alerts and sky localisation for follow-up
summary: A three-detector LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA network triangulates a merger from arrival-time differences and issues low-latency alerts. GW170817's 28 deg² error region let optical telescopes find its kilonova in NGC 4993 within 11 hours.
sources: LIGO, Virgo et al. (2017). "Multi-messenger Observations of a Binary Neutron Star Merger". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L12. [arXiv:1710.05833](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05833)

name: Binary-evolution channels behind GW mergers
summary: Isolated binary evolution (mass transfer, common envelope, supernova kicks) and dynamical assembly in clusters predict different merger rates, mass ratios and spin–orbit alignments. GW catalogues weigh these channels through rates and effective spins. The Peters inspiral time sets which binaries merge within a Hubble time.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Tidal deformability measures neutron-star radii
summary: In a neutron-star inspiral the tidal Love number enters the GW phase at 5PN order. GW170817 bounded the tidal deformability of a 1.4 M_sun star to Λ≲800, implying radii of ~11–13 km and ruling out the stiffest nuclear equations of state.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)

name: Pulsar timing probes ultralight dark matter
summary: Ultralight scalar ('fuzzy') dark matter has an oscillating pressure that makes the metric potentials oscillate at f=2mc²/h, in the nHz band for m~10⁻²³ eV, leaving coherent PTA residuals. PTAs also bound dark-matter substructure through the Doppler and Shapiro shifts of passing clumps.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)

name: nHz background from supermassive-black-hole binaries
summary: Hierarchical galaxy mergers pair up central black holes into binaries, whose combined inspiral predicts a nanohertz background with h_c∝f^{-2/3}. The amplitude PTAs reported in 2023 constrains SMBH mass functions, merger rates and how binaries get past the final-parsec problem.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Pulsar timing found the first exoplanets
summary: The timing model PTAs use fits pulse arrival times for Rømer delays, spin-down and noise. Applied to PSR B1257+12, it left periodic residuals that Wolszczan and Frail attributed to Earth-mass planets, the first confirmed exoplanets. The same residual analysis now searches for nanohertz gravitational waves.
sources: Wolszczan & Frail (1992). "A planetary system around the millisecond pulsar PSR1257 + 12". *Nature* 355, 145. [doi:10.1038/355145a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/355145a0)

name: Millisecond pulsars as a galactic GW detector
summary: Millisecond pulsars, spun up by accretion in binaries, are clocks stable to ~100 ns over decades. PTAs turn an ensemble of them into a galaxy-sized detector whose arms are pulsar–Earth baselines. Intrinsic spin noise and dispersion-measure variations are the main systematics.
sources: Hewish et al. (1968). "Observation of a Rapidly Pulsating Radio Source". *Nature* 217, 709. [doi:10.1038/217709a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/217709a0)
NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae
summary: A Galactic core-collapse supernova should emit a GW burst from proto-neutron-star oscillations, convection and SASI, with h~10⁻²¹–10⁻²² at 10 kpc. Current detectors reach only the Milky Way. Third-generation detectors such as Einstein Telescope would extend that reach and, alongside the neutrino burst, probe the explosion mechanism.

name: Loop quantum cosmology bounce before inflation
summary: Loop quantum cosmology replaces the big-bang singularity with a bounce at ρ_c≈0.41 ρ_Pl, using an effective Friedmann equation. The bounce sets pre-inflationary initial conditions and can suppress low-ℓ CMB power. These signatures depend on the model and are unconfirmed.

name: Vacuum energy and the cosmological constant problem
summary: Lorentz invariance forces the renormalised vacuum stress tensor into the form ⟨T_μν⟩=−ρ_vac c² g_μν, which gravitates exactly like Λ. Naive estimates of ρ_vac exceed the observed ~6×10⁻²⁷ kg m⁻³, about (2.3 meV)⁴, by up to ~120 orders of magnitude: the cosmological constant problem.
map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}c^2g_{\mu\nu}\ \Rightarrow\ \Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+\frac{8\pi G}{c^2}\rho_{\rm vac}
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The cosmological constant problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)

name: Quantum vacuum fluctuations seed cosmic structure
summary: Inflationary perturbations are QFT on a quasi-de Sitter background. Bunch–Davies vacuum fluctuations of the inflaton and the graviton are stretched beyond the horizon and freeze, becoming the nearly scale-invariant scalar spectrum (n_s≈0.965) and a tensor spectrum set by H/M_Pl.

name: CMB dipole: our motion through the relic radiation
summary: A Lorentz boost turns an isotropic blackbody into a blackbody whose temperature depends on direction. The 3.36 mK CMB dipole implies the Solar System moves at ~370 km/s, and Planck detected the accompanying aberration and Doppler modulation of the small-scale anisotropies. The CMB frame is a cosmological rest frame, not a violation of relativity.

name: Cosmological redshift vs special-relativistic Doppler
summary: At low z the cosmological redshift looks like a Doppler shift with v≈cz, and any FLRW redshift can be built from infinitesimal Doppler shifts parallel-transported along the photon path. The recession velocity in Hubble's law is not a Lorentz velocity, however.
breaks: Recession speeds v=Hd exceed c beyond the Hubble sphere, and z records the expansion between emission and reception, not a relative velocity in one inertial frame. Converting z to a velocity with the SR formula gives wrong distances at z≳0.5.

name: Cosmic-ray muons: time dilation observed
summary: Muons produced by cosmic rays ~15 km up reach sea level only because their 2.2 μs lifetime is dilated by γ~10–50. Rossi and Hall's 1941 measurement of muon flux against altitude was one of the first direct confirmations of relativistic time dilation.

name: Superluminal motion and Doppler boosting in jets
summary: Jet components moving at β≈1 close to our line of sight show apparent transverse speeds up to γβc, observed up to tens of c. Their flux is boosted by a high power of the Doppler factor δ, which is why blazars dominate the extragalactic gamma-ray sky.

name: Threshold kinematics: the GZK cutoff
summary: Cosmic-ray protons above ~5×10¹⁹ eV photoproduce pions on CMB photons. The threshold follows from the invariant s, and at Lorentz factors γ~10¹¹ these losses limit proton horizons to ~100 Mpc, which explains the observed flux suppression.
sources: Greisen (1966). "End to the Cosmic-Ray Spectrum?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 16, 748. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.748](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.16.748)

name: Compactness problem demands Γ≳100 outflows
summary: Millisecond GRB variability implies a tiny source, whose MeV photon density would be opaque to γγ→e⁺e⁻. The emitter must move with bulk Lorentz factor Γ≳100: beaming lowers comoving photon energies below pair threshold and enlarges the inferred emission radius by Γ².
sources: Mészáros (2006). "Gamma-ray bursts". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 69, 2259. [arXiv:astro-ph/0605208](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0605208)

name: GRB photon timing bounds Lorentz violation
summary: Quantum-gravity-motivated dispersion, v≈c(1−ξE/E_QG), would delay high-energy photons from cosmological GRBs relative to low-energy ones. Fermi-LAT timing of GRB 090510 pushed the linear-order scale E_QG past the Planck energy.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: GRMHD accretion models behind EHT images
summary: Ideal MHD in Kerr spacetime, with MRI-driven disk turbulence and ray-traced synchrotron emission, supplies the model libraries used to score EHT images of M87* and Sgr A*. Polarimetry favours magnetically arrested disks (MAD) over weakly magnetized (SANE) flows.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. V. Physical Origin of the Asymmetric Ring". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L5. [arXiv:1906.11242](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11242)
Balbus & Hawley (1991). "A Powerful Local Shear Instability in Weakly Magnetized Disks. I. Linear Analysis". *Astrophys. J.* 376, 214. [doi:10.1086/170270](https://doi.org/10.1086/170270)

name: Reconnection flares and plasmoids near horizons
summary: Near-infrared and X-ray flares of Sgr A*, and the orbiting hot spots seen by GRAVITY, are modelled as plasmoids from reconnecting equatorial current sheets during MAD flux eruptions. Electrons accelerated by the reconnection supply the emission.

name: Interstellar plasma turbulence blurs Sgr A*
summary: The image of Sgr A* is broadened by diffractive and refractive scattering in the turbulent ionized interstellar medium, whose Kolmogorov-like density spectrum is the footprint of the MHD cascade. EHT imaging must model the λ² scattering kernel and the refractive substructure.

name: Collisionless two-temperature accretion plasma
summary: Hot accretion flows onto Sgr A* and M87* are collisionless because Coulomb collision times exceed inflow times, so ions and electrons decouple. Electron heating by kinetic dissipation (Landau damping of the turbulent cascade, reconnection) sets the observed brightness; EHT models parametrize it with R_high.

name: Faraday rotation probes horizon-scale plasma
summary: Birefringence of the magnetized plasma rotates the EVPA by RM·λ². Rotation measures of M87* and Sgr A* constrain the accretion rate and field geometry, and internal Faraday rotation scrambles polarization in GRMHD models, which helps tell MAD from SANE flows.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2024). "First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results. VIII. Physical Interpretation of the Polarized Ring". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 964, L26. [doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ad2df1](https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ad2df1)

name: Transonic winds and acoustic/Alfvén horizons
summary: Parker's wind passes through a sonic critical point. This transonic flow is the time-reverse of Bondi accretion, whose sonic surface is an acoustic horizon in Unruh's analogue-gravity sense. The Alfvén critical surface, which Parker Solar Probe crossed in 2021, likewise cuts the outer wind off from the Sun for Alfvén waves.
breaks: The wind is an outflow, so its horizon is white-hole-like. Its critical point is set by gravity plus pressure rather than by geometry alone, and a 10⁶ K plasma swamps any analogue Hawking emission; only the classical causal structure carries over.
sources: Parker (1958). "Dynamics of the Interplanetary Gas and Magnetic Fields". *Astrophys. J.* 128, 664. [doi:10.1086/146579](https://doi.org/10.1086/146579)

name: Accelerating plasma mirrors as evaporation analogues
summary: Chen & Mourou proposed plasma mirrors, driven by a laser through graded-density plasma along tailored accelerating trajectories, as Fulling–Davies moving mirrors that emit Hawking-like thermal pairs. Correlations between partner photons could then test information loss; this is the AnaBHEL experiment.
breaks: A 1+1-dimensional moving mirror has no curvature, greybody factors or backreaction. The real plasma mirror is partly transparent and three-dimensional, and the signal is tiny against laser-plasma backgrounds, so it tests the kinematics of particle creation, not quantum gravity.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Grad–Shafranov and the relativistic stream equation
summary: Axisymmetric equilibria reduce to one nonlinear elliptic PDE for the poloidal flux: the Grad–Shafranov equation in tokamaks, and its relativistic force-free generalization in Kerr magnetospheres, the Blandford–Znajek stream equation (a relative of the pulsar equation). The free functions Ω_F(ψ) and I(ψ) play the roles of p(ψ) and F(ψ).

name: Blandford–Znajek: force-free extraction of Kerr spin
summary: A force-free (E·B=0) magnetosphere threading a spinning horizon carries outward Poynting flux paid for by the hole's rotational energy. It is the electromagnetic version of the Penrose process and the standard engine for AGN and GRB jets.
sources: Blandford & Znajek (1977). "Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 179, 433. [doi:10.1093/mnras/179.3.433](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/179.3.433)

name: Reconnection-driven Penrose process in the ergosphere
summary: Fast reconnection mediated by plasmoids inside the ergosphere can put one plasmoid on an orbit with negative energy at infinity and send the other to infinity, extracting spin energy. This reconnection variant of the Penrose process needs near-maximal spin and strong magnetization.

name: Black-hole shadow and lensing in a plasma
summary: In a cold plasma a photon behaves like a particle of mass ħω_p/c², so rays follow Synge's dispersive Hamiltonian instead of null geodesics. The photon sphere and the shadow size then depend on frequency: the effect is negligible at EHT's 230 GHz but significant at low radio frequencies.

name: GR particle-in-cell simulations of Kerr magnetospheres
summary: Particle-in-cell kinetics with pair creation has been ported to the Kerr metric. These simulations launch Blandford–Znajek jets from first principles and show spark-gap pair discharges near the horizon and kinetic reconnection in the equatorial current sheet.

name: Charged-particle orbits around magnetized black holes
summary: Wald's solution for a uniform field in Kerr spacetime allows gyration, drifts and adiabatic invariants to be studied in curved spacetime. The field shifts the ISCO, makes orbits chaotic and enables a magnetic Penrose process for charged particles.

name: Horizon as a unipolar inductor (membrane paradigm)
summary: A spinning horizon threaded by magnetic flux acts like a rotating conductor that generates an EMF ~Ω_HΦ, with the circuit closing through the magnetosphere. This is the same unipolar-inductor picture as the Io–Jupiter flux-tube circuit and pulsar magnetospheres; in the membrane paradigm the horizon has a surface resistivity of 377 Ω.
breaks: The horizon is a causal boundary, not a material conductor. Its 'resistivity' is a teleological boundary condition fixed by the metric, it carries no real charges, and the energy comes from negative-energy states in the ergosphere rather than from a moving body.

name: Gravitating 'plasma': Jeans instability and Einstein–Vlasov
summary: The Vlasov–Poisson system for self-gravitating collisionless matter (the Newtonian limit) is plasma kinetics with the sign of the interaction flipped. The squared plasma frequency turns negative, so oscillations become the Jeans instability, and gravitational Landau damping also exists. The relativistic version is the Einstein–Vlasov system.
breaks: With one-sign charge there is no Debye screening and no neutralizing background, hence the Jeans swindle. Self-gravitating systems are non-extensive, have negative heat capacity, and relax violently rather than towards Maxwellians.

name: Chameleon screening vs Debye screening
summary: Both cut off a 1/r force through a mass that depends on the environment. Debye shielding by mobile charges gives a Yukawa potential whose length λ_D is set by density and temperature. A chameleon scalar's effective mass grows with ambient density, so fifth forces are Yukawa-suppressed in dense environments.
breaks: Debye screening is the linear response of charges of both signs. Chameleon screening is a nonlinear self-interaction whose thin-shell suppression depends on the source's Newtonian potential. Vainshtein screening works through derivatives and involves no mass at all, and gravity itself, with one-sign charge, cannot be Debye-screened.

name: Field amplification in neutron-star mergers
summary: The Kelvin–Helmholtz instability at the contact layer of merging neutron stars drives a small-scale turbulent dynamo that amplifies fields toward magnetar strength within milliseconds, and an MRI dynamo follows in the remnant disk. This controls jet launching and outflows like GRB 170817A, but GRMHD resolves it only partly.

name: Constraint damping: ∇·B=0 vs Einstein constraints
summary: Both are hyperbolic evolutions that carry elliptic constraints, which hold analytically but drift numerically. Constraint damping in Z4/CCZ4 and generalized-harmonic codes and hyperbolic divergence cleaning in MHD use the same trick: turn the violation into a damped field that propagates away.
breaks: Einstein's constraints generate diffeomorphisms, so their violation mixes with the gauge choice. ∇·B=0 is a topological identity with no gauge content, and constrained transport can enforce it exactly, which has no GR counterpart.

name: GRMHD: ideal MHD on a dynamical spacetime
summary: Conservative shock-capturing schemes and constrained transport for ∇·B=0, first developed for Newtonian MHD, were carried into GR codes. The stress–energy of the magnetized fluid, including magnetic pressure and tension, sources Einstein's equations in simulations of neutron-star mergers and collapse.

name: Coronal plasma in solar-conjunction GR tests
summary: The dispersive delay of the corona and solar wind contaminates measurements of Shapiro delay and light deflection near the Sun. During its 2002 solar conjunction, Cassini's multi-frequency (X/Ka) link cancelled the plasma term and bounded γ−1=(2.1±2.3)×10⁻⁵.

name: Gravitational waves driving plasma waves
summary: A GW crossing a magnetized plasma shakes the field lines and can resonantly excite Alfvén and magnetosonic waves, or convert to EM waves (Gertsenshtein effect); this has been proposed as a merger counterpart. The GW itself is neither dispersed nor screened, because gravitational charge has one sign and there is no gravitational plasma frequency.

name: GW170817 afterglow from a relativistic collisionless shock
summary: The neutron-star merger GW170817 launched a structured relativistic jet whose radio-to-X-ray afterglow is synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated at its collisionless forward shock. Afterglow modelling (Blandford–McKee dynamics, ε_e, ε_B), combined with the inclination from the GW signal, fixed the viewing angle and explained the superluminal motion of the centroid.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)

name: Interstellar turbulence: scattering noise in timing
summary: Electron-density turbulence in the ISM, with a Kolmogorov spectrum, scatter-broadens pulses (∝ν^-4.4) and makes the DM wander. This strongly chromatic noise term in PTA analyses comes from the same turbulent medium studied as MHD turbulence.

name: Cold-plasma dispersion as PTA chromatic noise
summary: Radio pulses crossing the ionized ISM obey ω²=ω_p²+k²c² and arrive late by an amount ∝ DM/ν². Time-variable DM is a chromatic red noise that PTAs remove with multi-frequency timing, exposing the achromatic GW signal with its Hellings–Downs correlation.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Solar-wind electron density in PTA noise models
summary: Lines of sight that pass near the Sun pick up extra DM from the solar wind, so PTAs fit solar-wind density models (n_e∝r⁻² plus stochastic terms) to keep it from leaking into the GW background. In turn, PTA data constrain the solar-wind density.

name: GW backgrounds from primordial MHD turbulence
summary: A first-order phase transition at the electroweak scale stirs the ionized early-universe plasma into MHD turbulence, whose anisotropic stress sources a stochastic GW background in LISA's mHz band. The spectral shape depends on the cascade (Kolmogorov vs Iroshnikov–Kraichnan, decay laws), and the same process at the QCD scale is a candidate PTA source.

name: Test-mass charging by heliospheric particles
summary: The free-falling test masses of LISA-type detectors pick up charge from galactic cosmic rays, modulated by the solar wind, and from solar energetic particles driven by CME shocks, which produces Coulomb and Lorentz force noise. LISA Pathfinder measured this charging and removed it by UV photoemission.

name: MHD as higher-form hydrodynamics with holographic duals
summary: Magnetohydrodynamics has been recast as the hydrodynamics of a conserved two-form current, with magnetic flux lines as conserved strings. This extends it to strongly coupled plasmas without quasiparticles and admits holographic duals with a two-form field in the AdS bulk.

name: KSS viscosity bound and strongly coupled plasmas
summary: The value η/s≥ħ/4πk_B, derived from black-brane horizons, serves as a yardstick for 'perfect fluids'. Strongly coupled Coulomb and Yukawa plasmas (dusty and ultracold neutral plasmas) have a viscosity minimum where gas-like and liquid-like transport cross, and this minimum has been compared with the bound.
breaks: The bound is a conjecture, and holographic theories with higher-derivative terms violate it. Classical Coulomb plasmas are neither conformal nor quantum, ħ plays no role in their transport, and they sit far above the bound.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Probing Unruh radiation with ultra-intense lasers
summary: Electrons driven by laser fields with a₀≫1 reach proper accelerations at which the Unruh temperature is no longer negligible. Proposals (Chen & Tajima) look for its signature as a small extra emission beneath classical Larmor radiation, though whether such a signal can be told apart from ordinary radiation reaction is debated.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)

name: Relativistic flying mirrors: 4γ² frequency upshift
summary: Einstein's 1905 moving-mirror result, a double Doppler shift of ≈4γ², is realized by density cusps in wake waves and by laser-driven plasma surfaces oscillating at relativistic speed. Both are routes to coherent XUV/X-ray pulses and high harmonics.

name: Lorentz-boosted-frame simulation of accelerators
summary: The ratio of the longest to the shortest space and time scales is not Lorentz invariant. Simulating a laser–plasma accelerator in a frame moving near the wake phase velocity therefore collapses the scale disparity and cuts particle-in-cell cost by orders of magnitude.
sources: Vay (2007). "Noninvariance of Space- and Time-Scale Ranges under a Lorentz Transformation and the Implications for the Study of Relativistic Interactions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 130405. [doi:10.1103/physrevlett.98.130405](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.98.130405)

name: E×B drift is the frame where E vanishes
summary: For crossed fields with E<cB, a boost by v=E×B/B² removes E, so the guiding-centre drift is the velocity of that frame, and ideal Ohm's law E+v×B=0 states that the plasma rest frame has no electric field. When E>cB no such frame exists and particles run away, as in pulsar gaps.

name: Relativistic intensity: a₀≳1 and γ-mass optics
summary: When the normalized vector potential a₀ exceeds 1, the electron's quiver motion becomes relativistic. The γ-increased mass lowers the effective plasma frequency, which causes relativistic self-focusing above a critical power and makes overdense plasma relativistically transparent.

name: Dephasing and γ_φ² energy gain in wakefields
summary: A plasma wake moves at the laser's group velocity, with Lorentz factor γ_φ≈ω₀/ω_p. Transforming to the wake frame shows that the maximum energy gain scales as 2γ_φ²m_ec² and that relativistic electrons outrun the wake after a dephasing length, the basic design limit of laser wakefield accelerators.
sources: Tajima & Dawson (1979). "Laser Electron Accelerator". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 43, 267. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.267](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.267)

name: Relativistic jump conditions and Γ² boosts
summary: Relativistic shocks in GRBs and pulsar-wind nebulae obey Taub's relativistic Rankine–Hugoniot conditions: T^{μν} and particle flux are continuous across the shock. In Fermi acceleration the first crossing boosts a particle's energy by ~Γ² and later cycles by ~2, giving a universal index s≈2.2 instead of the non-relativistic 2.

name: Shock-accelerated particles bound Lorentz violation
summary: Synchrotron emission from ~PeV electrons accelerated at the Crab pulsar-wind termination shock, and photon arrival times from relativistic shocks in GRBs, give some of the tightest bounds on modified dispersion relations suppressed by the Planck energy.

name: Synchrotron radiation: light sources and the M87* ring
summary: The EHT's 1.3 mm emission is synchrotron radiation from relativistic electrons gyrating in magnetic fields near the horizon, governed by the same critical-frequency and polarization physics that light sources are engineered around. EHT polarimetry reads the synchrotron polarization pattern to map the geometry of the magnetic field.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Fourier-plane imaging: VLBI u-v coverage and MRI k-space
summary: An interferometer measures Fourier components (visibilities) of the sky, and MRI measures k-space samples of the magnetization, so both reconstruct images from sparse Fourier data using regularized or compressed-sensing inversion. Bracewell's projection-slice reconstructions in radio astronomy anticipated the mathematics of CT.

name: Wave blocking on currents as a white-hole horizon
summary: Surface waves travelling against a strengthening current stop where the current speed equals their group velocity, which in the acoustic-metric picture is a white-hole horizon. Water-tank experiments measured Hawking-like mode conversion with a thermal-like amplitude ratio, and wave blocking at tidal inlets and river mouths is the same effect in the ocean.
breaks: Water waves are strongly dispersive (no exact horizon or Lorentz symmetry) and damped by viscosity, and the experiments probe classical stimulated conversion; the spontaneous quantum emission is far too cold to measure.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Photon sphere and transition state as unstable bottlenecks
summary: The photon sphere is a normally hyperbolic invariant set of unstable orbits that separates capture from escape, like the dividing surface of transition-state theory in reaction dynamics. Its Lyapunov exponent sets the damping of eikonal quasinormal modes in the same way that the curvature of the barrier top sets the imaginary parts of quantized transition-state resonances.
breaks: The black-hole case is a single geodesic or linear wave on a fixed background, with no thermal ensemble or energy redistribution; reaction transition states live in many-dimensional phase space with recrossing and intramolecular energy flow.

name: Atom interferometry hunts screened fifth forces
summary: Chameleon and symmetron screening hide a scalar fifth force inside dense bodies behind a thin shell, but individual atoms in an ultra-high-vacuum chamber are unscreened. Atom-interferometric acceleration measurements near a source mass have therefore excluded much of the chameleon parameter space proposed to explain dark energy.

name: Junk radiation and geostrophic adjustment
summary: Both fields evolve hyperbolic equations from initial data that must satisfy elliptic conditions: the Einstein constraints, or geostrophic and nonlinear-normal-mode balance. Data that are off the physical slow manifold shed spurious fast waves (junk radiation in binary simulations, inertia–gravity waves in weather models) that must be discarded before results are trusted, and both fields use Berger–Oliger adaptive mesh refinement.
breaks: The Einstein constraints are exact identities that the evolution preserves, whereas atmospheric balance is approximate (small Rossby number) and not conserved; junk radiation leaves through the outer boundary, while unbalanced gravity waves can persist and are actively filtered.

name: Clocks and atom interferometers test redshift and the EP
summary: Pound and Rebka first measured gravitational redshift over 22.5 m; optical lattice clocks now resolve it across millimetres. Atom interferometers comparing two isotopes test the weak equivalence principle near 1e-12, and these are the same quantum devices used as gravimeters and timing references.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: Frame dragging read out by SQUIDs and Sagnac gyroscopes
summary: Gravity Probe B measured geodetic and frame-dragging precession by reading the London moment of spinning superconducting rotors with SQUID magnetometers. Ring-laser and atom-interferometric Sagnac gyroscopes, which are also quantum-sensing devices, have been proposed to detect the Lense–Thirring effect on the ground (GINGER).
sources: Everitt et al. (2011). "Gravity Probe B: Final Results of a Space Experiment to Test General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 221101. [arXiv:1105.3456](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.3456)

name: Relativistic geodesy: clocks measure the geopotential
summary: A clock's rate depends on the gravitational potential, so comparing optical clocks at the 1e-18 level resolves height differences of about 1 cm, turning a GR test into a geodetic probe of Earth's gravity field and mass redistribution. In the other direction, satellite tests of frame dragging (LAGEOS) are limited by how well Earth's mass distribution is modelled.
sources: Hafele & Keating (1972). "Around-the-World Atomic Clocks: Predicted Relativistic Time Gains". *Science* 177, 166. [doi:10.1126/science.177.4044.166](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.177.4044.166)

name: Earth's normal modes as a gravitational-wave antenna
summary: A GW's tidal acceleration drives the quadrupolar modes of an elastic body, the principle of Weber's bar. Dyson (1969) computed Earth's seismic response to a GW, and records of Earth's free oscillations have been used to bound the stochastic GW background; lunar seismic antennas are now proposed for the decihertz band.

name: Squeezed light beats the shot-noise limit in LIGO
summary: LIGO is the largest quantum sensor: shot noise enters through the vacuum at the dark port, so injecting squeezed vacuum (now frequency-dependent) lowers it, the same squeezed-state toolkit used in atomic magnetometers and clocks. The trade-off between shot noise and radiation-pressure noise defines the standard quantum limit that all continuous displacement sensors share.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)
Degen, Reinhard & Cappellaro (2017). "Quantum sensing". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 035002. [arXiv:1611.02427](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02427)

name: Laser-read oscillators in a thermal bath
summary: LIGO's test-mass suspensions and an optically trapped bead are both harmonic oscillators in a thermal bath, read out with light, whose displacement noise is fixed by the fluctuation–dissipation theorem. Optical tweezers are calibrated from the Lorentzian Brownian spectrum, and LIGO's thermal-noise budget comes from the mechanical loss entering the same formula.
breaks: LIGO works far above resonance, with tiny structural loss angles and quantum back-action, while a trapped bead is overdamped in water, classical, and probes forces rather than strain.

name: Ocean microseism as a GW-detector noise source
summary: Opposing ocean swells generate pressure fluctuations at twice the wave frequency (the Longuet-Higgins mechanism), which travel through the ground as the 0.1–0.3 Hz secondary microseism. This ground motion dominates the seismic input to LIGO and Virgo and causes lock losses during ocean storms, so it shapes their isolation and control design.

name: Newtonian noise and prompt elastogravity signals
summary: Seismic waves compress rock and so change local gravity. In GW detectors this Newtonian noise cannot be shielded and limits sensitivity below about 10 Hz, which is why the Einstein Telescope will be underground and why seismometer arrays are used for subtraction. In seismology the same effect produced prompt elastogravity signals, seen before the P-waves of the 2011 Tohoku earthquake.

name: SRF cavities as high-frequency GW detectors
summary: Superconducting RF cavities built for accelerators, with quality factors above 1e10, are being repurposed as heterodyne GW detectors. A passing high-frequency GW deforms the walls and couples to the field, pumping power between two nearly degenerate modes (the MAGO concept) and opening a kHz–GHz window beyond the reach of interferometers.
